note.text: Quantity asks universal or particular; quality asks affirmative or negative. No S are P is universal negative. Analyse both properties independently, then check what a rewrite preserves or changes.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to identify quantity and quality independently and explain which property changes in a rewrite. Builds on: categorical claims and their quantifiers. Leads to: combining the properties to recognise A, E, I and O.

sections.heading: Quantity asks how widely
sections.text: Universal propositions concern the entire subject class: All S are P and No S are P. Particular propositions assert at least one subject member: Some S are P and Some S are not P. Universal does not mean that every object in the world is included. It concerns the whole class named by the subject.

sections.heading: Quality asks whether membership is affirmed
sections.text: Affirmative propositions attribute membership: All S are P and Some S are P. Negative propositions deny it: No S are P and Some S are not P. Negative does not mean rude, undesirable or false. A negative statement can be polite and true. Notice that No is universal in quantity despite denying overlap.

sections.heading: Track a change precisely
sections.text: In an invented Bamenda club example, changing All members are readers to Some members are readers changes quantity while keeping affirmative quality. Changing Some members are readers to Some members are not readers changes quality while keeping particular quantity. Classify each property separately before combining them; the next lesson names the resulting patterns.

key_words.meaning: asserting at least one subject member

mistake.right: No S are P is universal and negative.
mistake.why: It rules out overlap for the entire subject class.

worked_example.problem: Analyse Some library books are not loanable items.
steps: Some asserts at least one subject member: particular quantity.
Are not denies membership: negative quality.
Keep these two properties separate before naming the whole form.

cards.idea: All and no are universal; some is particular.
example: No school gardens are cultivated areas is universal in quantity, even if factually false.
Some S are P affirms; Some S are not P denies membership.

cards.idea: Changing all to some changes scope, not affirmation.
example: All S are P and Some S are P remain affirmative.

pick.q: Bih changes “All club members are badge holders” to “Some club members are badge holders.” What changes?
e: All becomes some, changing scope rather than affirmation.
Neither sentence denies membership.
The universal-to-particular change is significant.
pick.y: All and some differ in quantity, while both sentences affirm membership.

questions.prompt: Find the incorrect claim, then read the reason for the correction.

right.text: Quantity distinguishes universal and particular scope.
right.explain: This is a correct rule: Quantity distinguishes universal and particular scope. Look for a claim that breaks a rule taught in Learn.
This is a correct rule: Quality distinguishes affirmation and denial. Look for a claim that breaks a rule taught in Learn.

right.text: No S are P is universal and negative.
right.explain: This is a correct rule: No S are P is universal and negative. Look for a claim that breaks a rule taught in Learn.

right.text: Some S are P is particular and affirmative.
right.explain: This is a correct rule: Some S are P is particular and affirmative. Look for a claim that breaks a rule taught in Learn.

wrong.text: No S are P is particular because it contains no objects.
wrong.explain: No covers the whole subject class by denying any overlap; it is universal in quantity.

wrong.text: A negative proposition must be an insulting remark.
wrong.explain: Negative is a logical denial of membership, not a description of politeness.
Some S are P is particular and affirmative.

wrong.text: All and some differ only in spelling, without a change in scope.
wrong.explain: All concerns the whole subject class; some asserts at least one member.
